feature: Customer Portal v2 -- the OWNERSHIP matrix (/portal-v2/ownership), now reading REAL TENANT DATA from GET /api/portal/ownership instead of the ownershipData.ts design fixture. Four names (Responsible / Accountable / Consulted / Informed) against the customer's own objects: their purchased services, their Microsoft changes with an action still due, their change requests, and their open hold windows -- plus the people list, which is their own active users. This manifest proves the DOM shows what the ENDPOINT returned, not what a fixture contains: every row id, person id and person name it asserts against is EXTRACTED FROM THE API RESPONSE at run time and interpolated into the selector, so the test cannot pass against a stale fixture and does not have to be re-pinned when the tenant's data changes. It ALSO proves the matrix's WRITE actions now persist: a cell assigned through the real POST route is read back off the matrix after a full page reload (API7-API9 + OWN49-OWN50).
notes: THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute; a probe that skips the five login steps hits the login screen and every assertion fails for a reason unrelated to the page.

UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/ownership. App.tsx declares '/portal-v2/ownership/:type' and '/portal-v2/ownership' BEFORE '/portal-v2/:pillar' so the param route cannot swallow them.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree. This manifest cannot pass until the commit it was written against is deployed.

WHY THE FIXTURE NUMBERS ARE GONE. The previous version of this manifest asserted '24 of 24 shown', '6 ownership gaps', '3 duty conflicts' and named cells like pv2-own-cell-svc-exo-r / 'Priya Raman'. Every one of those was a property of the DESIGN FIXTURE (the prototype's fictional Halden Materials estate), and none of them survives the page reading a real tenant. They are replaced by assertions that extract the tenant's OWN first object id/name, change-request code and person id/name from the API response and then assert the DOM against those -- which is the pattern CLAUDE.md prescribes (apiTests + uiStep textContains) and is a STRONGER test: it fails if the page falls back to the fixture, which the old assertions could not detect.

WHAT IS REAL AND WHAT IS NOT, so a reader does not over-read a green run. REAL: the matrix rows, the people list, and the Responsible/Accountable cells on a change request -- its requester and its approver, the only two owner names the schema stores for anything. NOT REAL, and asserted AS gaps rather than hidden: Consulted and Informed on every row, and Responsible/Accountable on everything that is not a change request. There is no ownership/RACI table in the database (an information_schema sweep for owner/assigned/responsible columns finds nothing about these objects), so those cells are genuinely unassigned. OWN6 asserts one of them shows the word 'Assign', which is what the page renders for a gap -- i.e. the gap is proved on screen, not assumed.

THE THREE ABSENT GROUPS ARE AN ASSERTION, NOT AN OMISSION. control / incident / announce have no table behind them, so the endpoint returns them as sources with live:false and no rows, and the matrix renders no group for them. OWN11-OWN13 pin that, and the apiTest pins the endpoint's own live:false claim, so a future build that invents rows for them fails here rather than shipping quietly.

OWN5 DEPENDS ON THE TESTBED ACCOUNT BEING THE REQUESTER, and says so rather than hiding it. Every change request in this tenant was raised by TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL, so the endpoint's own currentUserName is also the Responsible name on those rows, which is what makes the assertion self-describing (it is extracted, not hardcoded). If a future tenant's CRs are raised by someone else, re-point OWN5 at that person's name -- the step is still asserting a REAL owner either way.

THE PROP CONTRACT IS STILL PROVED ACROSS TWO PAGES, and now over real people. OWN27-OWN31 rename the REAL user who owns the real change requests in Settings, then read the new name out of the Ownership matrix. That is the README's 'the Ownership matrix reads the same data live', and it is the one assertion that would fail if the people list were forked into a second source when it was wired to the endpoint.

OWN30 MUST BE A CLICK, NOT A `goto`, AND A PREVIOUS RUN PROVED IT. `goto` is a FULL PAGE LOAD, which resets the client store and re-reads the endpoint -- so the rename would be gone and the step would test the fetch rather than the sharing. That is correct behaviour, not a bug: there is still no people/roles WRITE endpoint and no table to persist a rename to, so edits live for the session exactly as the prototype's do. The sidebar nav row is a client-side wouter Link, so clicking it preserves the store and is also how a customer actually gets there. WHEN A REAL PEOPLE WRITE ENDPOINT LANDS, this step can become a `goto` and should then still pass; if it does not, the persistence is not wired.

OWN28 ASSERTS `state` AND NOT TEXT, deliberately: pv2-set-person-name-* is an <input>, whose innerText/textContent is empty regardless of its value, so a textContains there would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the data. The NAME is asserted through the API (the person id it interpolates came from the response) and through OWN31, where it reaches the matrix as real rendered text.

THERE IS NO NEGATIVE TEXT ASSERTION IN THIS HARNESS, and an array in `textContains` is ANY-of, not all-of (UiTestExecutor.cs:570, :1282). Every all-of assertion here is its own step, and absence is asserted on a selector rather than on text.

NO `select` STEPS ANYWHERE. UiTestExecutor.cs takes the `value` setter from HTMLInputElement.prototype for anything that is not a TEXTAREA, so invoking it on a native <select> throws 'Illegal invocation'; and an unrecognised action falls through and SILENTLY PASSES. This page has no <select> in its main flow.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD.

WRITE PERSISTENCE (API7-API9 + OWN49-OWN50). The matrix's mutations -- assign, mark-accepted, handover, add-a-row -- were React state only and lost on reload; the route called itself 'Read-only, deliberately'. Three per-customer tables now back them (portal_ownership_assignments / portal_ownership_delegations / portal_ownership_rows), the GET returns an `overlay` block, and the client seeds its state from it. API8 assigns the CR's CONSULTED cell (a role the read never fills, so a name there can only be from the overlay), and OWN50 -- after a FULL page reload (OWN49 goto) -- reads that name back off the matrix. That is the round trip end to end: POST persists -> GET overlay returns it -> the reloaded UI renders it. WHY CONSULTED AND NOT ACCOUNTABLE: OWN6 asserts the CR's Accountable cell reads 'Assign' (a gap), and the write is idempotent + persistent, so assigning -a would break OWN6 on the next run; -c is asserted nowhere else and is a gap by nature, so it is the clean target.

STILL SESSION-ONLY, and honestly so: 'Accept it unowned' (the risk toggle). It is not one of the assign/handover/add flows this pass wired, and the route header says so. Also NOT re-tested here: that a client-side nav (not a full reload) preserves an in-session ownership edit -- the store overlay is refreshed from the DB only on a full read, so a same-session edit reappears after a full reload (OWN49/OWN50) but a wouter-Link nav back re-seeds from the load-time overlay. That matches the pre-existing behaviour (ownership edits were always lost on unmount) and is not a regression; OWN49 uses a full goto deliberately.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated TESTBED account; extract the bearer.
API1 -- the route exists, admits a CustomerUser, and resolved the MSP-era tenant scope rather than failing closed to a half payload.
API2 -- the matrix has real rows; take the first row's NAME to assert against the DOM.
API3 -- a real change-request code, pulled off the payload by regex rather than by array index, since the type order within objects[] is a property of the data.
API4 -- the signed-in user resolved to a person in the tenant's own roster (this is also the requester on every CR here).
API5 -- ...and their real name, which is what the matrix cell has to render.
API6 -- the endpoint STATES that the control register has no source, rather than returning an empty group and leaving the page to explain it.

API7 -- WRITE side: the read now carries an `overlay` block (the customer's own saved edits), returned as an array even when empty. Its presence is what lets the client seed assign/acceptance/handover/added-row state from real data on load.

API8 -- WRITE side: assign the change request's Consulted cell to the signed-in person through the real POST route. Consulted is a role the READ never fills (c/i are always gaps), so a name landing there later can only have come from the overlay -- which makes the reload assertion below a clean persistence proof. Idempotent: the route upserts on (customer, object, role), so re-runs overwrite rather than accumulate.

API9 -- ...and the route echoes what it saved: the cell it wrote is Consulted (roleKey 'c'), which carries no acceptance (only r/a do). Proves the write computed acceptance per-role rather than starting every cell pending.

API10 (#1517) -- a SECOND, distinct holder joins the same Consulted cell (the gap owner "" is itself a valid distinct holder under the #1515 unique key). It is appended at the END of the cell's precedence rather than replacing API8's holder -- order 1, not 0.

API11 (#1517) -- re-asserting API8's ORIGINAL holder (same objectId/roleKey/ownerPersonId) overwrites that row's provenance but leaves its precedence exactly where it was -- still order 0, not bumped to the end.
API12 (#1517) -- REORDER: flip the cell's precedence so the gap holder "" leads and the real person is second. Precedence only -- this changes nothing about who may act, only the informational order.

API13 (#1517) -- REORDER PERSISTED: read the overlay back and confirm the gap holder is now rank 0 for this cell -- the reorder wrote through to the same table the GET reads, not just to the response it echoed.
API14 (#1517) -- ...and the real person's holder in that same cell moved to rank 1, so the reorder is a genuine swap, not both rows independently defaulting to 0.
API15 (#1517) -- a reorder that omits one of the cell's real current holders is rejected rather than silently corrupting the omitted row's rank.

It is on screen only because the assignment was PERSISTED (portal_ownership_assignments) and the reload seeded the matrix from the overlay. Before this build every ownership mutation was React state and this cell would read 'Assign' again after a refresh.
